label: D. Scarlatti: Fugue in D minor, K. 417
caution: Read by the program from a typeset edition, notes and voices both. The notes were proofread against Gilbert's edition (Heugel) on 2026-11-23 and corrected; the voices are the program's, and some lines are in the wrong one (the entries of bars 15 and 22 share the soprano).
title: Domenico Scarlatti: Sonata in D minor, K. 417 (Fuga)
procedures: a voice held back until after the exposition

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Free counterpoint: nothing here is traced to the themes.
sections.leads: From D minor to A minor

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 13–14), with the alto's line in the soprano, at the same pitch level. Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted (4 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Bass: a figure from the subject (3 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Returns in Episode 3 (bars 59–123). Returns in Episode 6 (bars 193–238).
sections.leads: From A minor to D minor

sections.label: Episode 2
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 13–14) in part, with alto and bass exchanged, the lines moved by different intervals. Soprano: a figure from the subject (3 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a third every bar. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and a figure from the subject. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times) and a figure from the subject and the opening of the subject.
sections.leads: From D minor to F major

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 1 (bars 28–36), with the soprano's line in the alto, the alto's line in the soprano, the bass's line in the tenor, at the same pitch level. Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted (11 times) and a figure from the subject (7 times) and the opening of the subject (2 times) and the opening of the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (11 times) and a figure from the subject (7 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted (8 times) and a figure from the subject (7 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Bass: a figure from the subject (6 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times) and the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence rising by a step every two bars.
sections.leads: From F major to D minor; perfect cadence in C major at bar 119

sections.label: Subject in D minor (Tenor, its first entry)
Episode 4
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times) and the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (4 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Tenor: the opening of countersubject 1, inverted (7 times) and a figure from countersubject 2 (4 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted and the opening of countersubject 2, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars.
sections.leads: From D minor to A minor

sections.label: Episode 5
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 13–14) in part, in the same voices, the lines moved by different intervals. Soprano: a figure from the subject (2 times) and the opening of the subject (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 and a figure from countersubject 2 and a figure from the subject, in a sequence falling by a third every two bars. Tenor: the opening of countersubject 1, inverted (5 times) and a figure from countersubject 2 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a step every bar.
sections.leads: From A minor to D minor

sections.label: Episode 6
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 1 (bars 28–36) in part, in the same voices, a step lower. Soprano: a figure from the subject (6 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (4 times) and a figure from countersubject 2 (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 2, inverted (3 times) and the opening of countersubject 2 and the opening of the subject, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from the subject (5 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (5 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 (5 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Tenor: the opening of countersubject 1, inverted and a figure from countersubject 2 and a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: a figure from countersubject 2 (6 times) and the opening of countersubject 1, inverted (5 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars.
sections.leads: Perfect cadence in D minor at bar 222; perfect cadence in D minor at bar 237; perfect cadence in D minor at bar 239

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted. Bass: a figure from the subject. Returns in Episode 1 (bars 28–36). Returns in Episode 2 (bars 43–52). Returns in Episode 5 (bars 157–188).
